images.prompt: In the style of Tim Jacobus, a vertical book-cover illustration inspired by classic 1990s Goosebumps horror art. A monstrous supernatural entity made of swirling green ectoplasm emerges from an old beige computer screen, reaching toward the viewer with translucent, glowing fingers. The digital demon: A face-like apparition materializes from the monitor not quite human, not quite machine. Its features shift and ripple like liquid light, with glowing green "eyes" that seem to follow you and a wide, too-friendly smile made of flowing digital code. The entity appears curious and inviting rather than terrifying like it genuinely wants to be your friend, which makes it even more unsettling. Ectoplasmic emergence: Thick, luminous green slime pours from the computer screen like supernatural syrup, pooling on the desk and dripping toward the floor. The ectoplasm has a translucent, jelly-like quality similar to Monster Blood vibrant and almost appetizing, but clearly unnatural. Wisps of the green substance float in the air like digital smoke. The vintage computer: A chunky, yellowed desktop computer from the late 1980s sits on a kid's desk, its boxy CRT monitor and tower looking innocent and nostalgic. The machine appears almost toy-like in its simplicity, making the supernatural emergence even more jarring. Interactive menace: Tendrils of green ectoplasm stretch from the screen toward scattered homework papers, a computer mouse, and other desk items suggesting the entity is actively trying to connect with and manipulate the physical world. Some papers appear to be dissolving or changing as the supernatural substance touches them. Kid's bedroom setting: A typical middle-schooler's room fades into purple-blue twilight behind the computer. Unmade bed, backpack, school supplies, and posters on the walls all rendered in that distinctive Jacobus style where ordinary objects seem ominous in the eerie lighting. Classic Goosebumps palette: Electric lime greens contrasted with deep purples and midnight blues. The green ectoplasm glows brilliantly against the darker background, creating that perfect "scary but safe" atmosphere that defined 90s children's horror. Jacobus signature style: Airbrushed realism with bold outlines, dramatic lighting, and that unmistakable ability to make the fantastic seem tangible. The composition suggests an entity that desperately wants friendship and connection making it more psychologically unsettling than traditionally frightening. The overall effect captures the book's central theme: a supernatural being that presents itself as the perfect friend, but whose true nature seeps through in unsettling ways. Pure nostalgic tech-horror with classic Goosebumps charm. --chaos 25 --ar 1:1 --sref --stylize 550 --v 6.1

A heavy gold chain and the bottom edge of a large ruby medallion dangle just into frame from above, glinting. The figure's face is deliberately out of frame - cropped above the shorts - so we never see it, only the languid, predatory ease of a monster on vacation. Setting: a glittering turquoise resort pool shimmers in the background, slightly out of focus, with palm trees, a white stucco hotel, and an empty swan pool-float drifting on the water. Uncanny detail: though the scene is flooded with bright afternoon sun, the vampire's pale skin casts a faint cold shadow, and there is no reflection of the hand or legs in the pool's mirror-still water behind them. Jacobus signature style: airbrushed realism with bold outlines, dramatic sunlit lighting, glossy tangible textures on the sweating glass and pale skin. images.prompt: In the style of Tim Jacobus, a vertical book-cover illustration inspired by classic 1990s Goosebumps horror art. A monstrous supernatural entity made of swirling green ectoplasm emerges from an old beige computer screen, reaching toward the viewer with translucent, glowing fingers. - The digital demon: A face-like apparition materializes from the monitor - not quite human, not quite machine. Its features shift and ripple like liquid light, with glowing green "eyes" that seem to follow you and a wide, too-friendly smile made of flowing digital code. The entity appears curious and inviting rather than terrifying - like it genuinely wants to be your friend, which makes it even more unsettling. - Ectoplasmic emergence: Thick, luminous green slime pours from the computer screen like supernatural syrup, pooling on the desk and dripping toward the floor. The ectoplasm has a translucent, jelly-like quality similar to Monster Blood - vibrant and almost appetizing, but clearly unnatural. Wisps of the green substance float in the air like digital smoke. - The vintage computer: A chunky, yellowed desktop computer from the late 1980s sits on a kid's desk, its boxy CRT monitor and tower looking innocent and nostalgic. The machine appears almost toy-like in its simplicity, making the supernatural emergence even more jarring. - Interactive menace: Tendrils of green ectoplasm stretch from the screen toward scattered homework papers, a computer mouse, and other desk items - suggesting the entity is actively trying to connect with and manipulate the physical world. Some papers appear to be dissolving or changing as the supernatural substance touches them. - Kid's bedroom setting: A typical middle-schooler's room fades into purple-blue twilight behind the computer. Unmade bed, backpack, school supplies, and posters on the walls - all rendered in that distinctive Jacobus style where ordinary objects seem ominous in the eerie lighting. - Classic Goosebumps palette: Electric lime greens contrasted with deep purples and midnight blues. The green ectoplasm glows brilliantly against the darker background, creating that perfect "scary but safe" atmosphere that defined 90s children's horror. - Jacobus signature style: Airbrushed realism with bold outlines, dramatic lighting, and that unmistakable ability to make the fantastic seem tangible. The composition suggests an entity that desperately wants friendship and connection - making it more psychologically unsettling than traditionally frightening. The overall effect captures the book's central theme: a supernatural being that presents itself as the perfect friend, but whose true nature seeps through in unsettling ways. Pure nostalgic tech-horror with classic Goosebumps charm. --chaos 25 --ar 3:4 --sref --stylize 550 --v 6.1

images.prompt: In the style of Tim Jacobus, a vertical book-cover illustration inspired by classic 1990s Goosebumps horror art. An intimate, close-up composition at a luxurious Mexican beach resort in Cabo San Jose. The focal point: a single long, pale white hand reaching lazily toward the viewer from the arm of a poolside lounge chair, fingers unnaturally long and tapering to sharp filed points like soft claws, the skin the waxy bluish-white of a candle, casually gesturing "come here." In the foreground on a small side table, a margarita glass holds a thick, dark, blood-red liquid - clearly not a normal drink, opaque and deep crimson like fresh blood, glistening, a single slow red droplet running down the salted rim; a lime wedge and a tiny paper umbrella sit incongruously in the gore-red liquid, making it more unsettling. Beyond the reaching hand, the lower half of the reclining vampire: two impossibly long, hairless, candle-white legs on the lounger, bare feet with long toenails filed to points, and loud toucan-print Bermuda shorts in garish orange-sherbet. A heavy gold chain and the bottom edge of a large ruby medallion dangle into frame from above. The face is deliberately cropped out of frame above the shorts - we never see it. Setting, unmistakably a Mexican resort: an infinity pool overlooking the ocean, terracotta-tiled poolside, a thatched palapa umbrella with a dried-palm roof, tall palm trees, bright pink and magenta bougainvillea flowers spilling over white stucco walls, a distant white mission-style bell tower, string lights, and warm golden Baja sunlight. A brightly colored resort towel is draped over the lounger. Uncanny detail: bright afternoon sun floods everything, yet the still turquoise pool water holds no reflection of the hand or the legs. Classic Goosebumps palette: deep blood-reds and ruby crimsons (the drink, the medallion) against turquoise pool-blues, terracotta oranges, hot-pink bougainvillea, and sun-bleached whites. Jacobus signature style: airbrushed realism, bold outlines, glossy tangible textures on the sweating glass, the blood-red liquid, and pale skin. The composition captures the book's theme through implication - a monster so at home in paradise he doesn't sit up to greet you. Pure nostalgic sun-drenched vampire horror with classic Goosebumps charm. --chaos 10 --ar 3:4 --sref --stylize 0 --weird 8 --v 6.1

images.prompt: In the style of Tim Jacobus, a vertical book-cover illustration inspired by classic 1990s Goosebumps horror art. An intimate, close-up composition at a luxurious Mexican beach resort in Cabo San Jose. The focal point: a single long, pale white hand reaching lazily toward the viewer from the arm of a poolside lounge chair, fingers unnaturally long and tapering to sharp filed points like soft claws, the skin the waxy bluish-white of a candle, casually gesturing "come here." In the foreground on a small side table, a margarita glass holds a thick, dark, blood-red liquid - clearly not a normal drink, opaque and deep crimson like fresh blood, glistening, a single slow red droplet running down the salted rim; a lime wedge and a tiny paper umbrella sit incongruously in the gore-red liquid, making it more unsettling. Beyond the reaching hand, the lower half of the reclining vampire: two impossibly long, hairless, candle-white legs on the lounger, bare feet with long toenails filed to points, and loud toucan-print Bermuda shorts in garish orange-sherbet. A heavy gold chain and the bottom edge of a large ruby medallion dangle into frame from above. The face is deliberately cropped out of frame above the shorts - we never see it. Setting, unmistakably a Mexican resort: an infinity pool overlooking the ocean, terracotta-tiled poolside, a thatched palapa umbrella with a dried-palm roof, tall palm trees, bright pink and magenta bougainvillea flowers spilling over white stucco walls, a distant white mission-style bell tower, string lights, and warm golden Baja sunlight. A brightly colored resort towel is draped over the lounger. Uncanny detail: bright afternoon sun floods everything, yet the still turquoise pool water holds no reflection of the hand or the legs. Classic Goosebumps palette: deep blood-reds and ruby crimsons (the drink, the medallion) against turquoise pool-blues, terracotta oranges, hot-pink bougainvillea, and sun-bleached whites. Jacobus signature style: airbrushed realism, bold outlines, glossy tangible textures on the sweating glass, the blood-red liquid, and pale skin. The composition captures the book's theme through implication - a monster so at home in paradise he doesn't sit up to greet you. Pure nostalgic sun-drenched vampire horror with classic Goosebumps charm. --chaos 10 --ar 3:4 --sref --stylize 0 --weird 8 --v 6.1

Classic tropical-horror menace: At his feet in the wet sand rests a small, child-sized coffin of dark polished wood with brass corners and a curling letter "V" engraved on the lid, the lid open just a crack with darkness inside. Classic Goosebumps palette: Electric blood-reds and ruby crimsons contrasted with deep purples, midnight blues, and sickly moonlit whites.
